close_reason: Landed reviewed regression proof in 02aedeb88: AssertSame remains a constraint, equal allocations remain distinct, interpreter/JIT/AOT and Elixir oracle agree; focused tests, fmt, check, strict Clippy green.
description:
## Goal

Treat runtime equality assertions as constraints only. `AssertSame { source, value }` reads two already-defined values and proves they are semantically equal; it must not create a physical/value-origin definition edge in either direction.

## Proven defect

Accepted fz-kdt.27 correctly gives `AssertSame` no origin. During the ticket-scoped adversarial review of the uncommitted fz-tfn.64 generalization, this valid production program exposed a regression and stack-overflowed on interpreter, JIT, and AOT:

```fz
fn main() do
  x = 42
  ^x = x
  x
end
```

`ExecutableFacts::step_transport_origins` records `value -> LocalValue(source)` for `AssertSame`. Here both operands are the same existing value, producing a self-cycle in downstream origin traversal. More generally, structurally equal but separately allocated values satisfy equality without sharing allocation identity, so the edge is false even when it is acyclic.

The candidate regression is not a missing cycle guard: `AssertLiteral`, `AssertStruct`, `AssertTuple`, `AssertEmptyList`, `AssertSame`, and `AssertBitstringDone` define no values. `step_defined_values` already models that distinction correctly. Existing ticket and open-PR searches found no owner; closed fz-rh2.21.8 concerns semantic type-plane collapse, not value-origin identity. This ticket lands the durable structural and three-door regression proof on the accepted base before fz-tfn.64 generalizes origin collection; the actual one-line deletion remains part of that generalization.

## Correct model

Definitions create origins; constraints only read and refine existing definitions. Equality may refine semantic facts, establish reachability, or fail at runtime, but it does not prove denotational or physical identity and must not participate in ownership, transport, keying, or retention origin graphs.

Keep `AssertSame` absent from origin collection as that code is generalized. Do not reverse it, merge the values, add a cycle guard, canonicalize through display text, or create an equality-origin side table. Preserve existing equality semantics and demand reads of both operands.

This remains body-local derived information. It adds no World fact, ProductMemo product, pass, cache, or invalidation authority.

## TDD signal

The durable proof is intentionally narrow:

- a structural compiler test lowers equal, independently constructed lists through `AssertSame`, proves the operands have distinct `ValueId`s, and proves origin collection does not define or alias either operand;
- the existing equality/identity oracle fixture gains the exact self-pin cycle trigger and the equal-but-distinct list case, and must agree with Elixir on interpreter, JIT, and standalone AOT;
- the uncommitted fz-tfn.64 candidate is the historical RED: the false origin insertion fails the structural test and stack-overflows the self-pin on all three doors; deleting only that insertion makes both proofs green.

Existing equality fixtures continue to own unequal-match behavior. fz-tfn.64 owns broader ownership, retained-product, deterministic-artifact, and exact-work acceptance. Run the focused structural test, three-door fixture, Elixir oracle gate, formatting, check, strict Clippy, and a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review.

## Strategy and deletion

1. Preserve the candidate's production stack-overflow RED as historical evidence.
2. Land one structural origin assertion and one three-door semantic fixture on the accepted base.
3. In fz-tfn.64, delete only the false origin insertion and rerun this proof.
4. Remove temporary probes and avoid duplicate fixtures before each commit.

This prerequisite intentionally changes tests only; fz-tfn.64 contains the corresponding production deletion. One ticket, one commit, one close, then push only after the preceding stack head is green.

## Ordering

This is a P1 regression-proof prerequisite discovered while reviewing fz-tfn.64. It blocks fz-tfn.64 so that the larger outcome/ownership cutover is reviewed atop a correct acyclic definition graph. It otherwise introduces no new ordering edge.
title: Keep equality assertions out of the value-origin graph
